chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abū al-Ḥasan, from his father, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Mu‘āwiya ibn ‘Ammār, who said:
Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: Whatever you trample, or your camel tramples upon, while you are in iḥrām, then upon you is its ransom.

And he (peace be upon him) said: Know that there is no ransom upon you for anything you come to, while you are ignorant of it and you are in iḥrām during your Ḥajj, nor during your ‘Umra, except for the hunted prey; for upon you regarding it is the ransom, whether it was out of ignorance or deliberate.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.فِدَاء: Ransom or compensation offered for a specific act or item

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on ransom (fidyah) for a person in Ihram who hunts or tramples on prey?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between accidental contact with non-prey items and the specific liability for hunting (sayd) while in iḥrām. It establishes that while ignorance exempts one from ransom for general items, hunting requires a fidya (ransom) regardless of whether the act was committed out of ignorance (jahala) or deliberately (amdan), highlighting the strictness of preserving the sanctity of the Haram. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of the hunting prohibition even for those unaware of the specific prey.
